feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 8 (kp 3.0, kd 0.45, geometry as iteration 7) scored 610.7, with oval 20/20, s-bend 15/20 (line-loss 1.05) and slalom 0/20 (line-loss 1.9). Iteration 9 (kd 0.6) scored 669.8, with oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20 (line-loss 0.75) and slalom line-loss 1.1 with 0/20 finishes. Oval steering_oscillation stayed at about 0.22 across both steps, so the controller change did not cause jitter. Geometry tests from iterations 2 to 7 (span, footprint, forward position, wheel_track, mass) moved the sharp tracks only as the controller changed, so the body is not the constraint. The Integrator's controller step in this iteration is kd 0.6 to 0.75 with the geometry held. Decision rules for the next race: (a) If the oval holds at 20/20 or 16/20 or better and slalom line-loss falls below 1.1 with s-bend at 20/20 or 19/20, the geometry is stable and should be held for the final iteration. (b) If the oval falls below about 16/20 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35 with low max_error, the derivative gain is too high for this body, so keep geometry and return kd to 0.6. (c) If slalom stays near 1.1 line-loss with the oval and s-bend holding, geometry is still not the gap, so do not change sensors, span or wheel_track; the remaining lever is line_loss mode on the controller side.
requested_changes: Hold every geometry value at the iteration 9 best: wheel_track 0.09 m, span ±0.03 m at 0.015 m spacing, sensor y 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.5 kg, body 0.12 x 0.16 m. Evidence: iteration 9 scored 669.8 on this geometry, and every geometry change since iteration 4 has been flat or negative on the sharp tracks, while controller changes have moved the sharp-track line-loss.

If the oval holds at 16/20 or better and slalom line-loss is at or below 1.1 per run after kd 0.75, keep this geometry for the final iteration without change. Evidence: kd 0.45 to 0.6 cut slalom line-loss from 1.9 to 1.1 with the oval unchanged, which shows the controller response is still moving the sharp tracks.

If the next race shows the oval dropping below about 16/20 with steering_oscillation above about 0.35, do not change geometry. Return kd to 0.6, the iteration 9 value, and keep wheel_track 0.09 m. Evidence: mass and wheel_track changes did not cause jitter at 0.5 kg, so a jitter rise would point to the controller, not the body.
